The Office of Personnel Management issued a direct final rule making technical revisions to its Family and Medical Leave Act regulations.

The rule incorporates statutory changes that make virtually all Federal civilian service and certain honorable active military service count toward the 12-month FMLA eligibility requirement.

It also clarifies that annual and sick leave provided under authorities outside title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, and it excludes certain Veterans Health Administration employees from title 5 FMLA coverage.

Because paid parental leave is substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, the rule also affects eligibility for Federal paid parental leave.

The rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rule.
